title: Cumulative retrieval quiz
subject: English
unit: Spring 2: Julius Caesar (Shakespeare): leadership, persuasion and responsibility
source: Seeded from english/y8 lesson 44 (Cumulative retrieval quiz (portal))
intro: Covers lessons 29 to 48 of Julius Caesar (Shakespeare): leadership, persuasion and responsibility. Answer every question. For multiple choice, fill in one circle.

questions.q: Why do the tribunes remove decorations from Caesar's statues?
options: They fear Caesar is becoming too powerful
questions.a: B) They fear Caesar is becoming too powerful. They want to stop Caesar 'soaring' above others; the other options misread the scene.

questions.q: Why does the writer use the captain anecdote?
options: To tell a true news story
To prove captains are always women
To make an abstract quality concrete and memorable
questions.a: C) To make an abstract quality concrete and memorable. An anecdote humanises the argument; the other options misread its purpose.

questions.q: Which uses nominalisation?
questions.a: A) Brutus's decision divides Rome.. 'decision' turns the verb into a noun; the other options keep verbs.

questions.q: Why is 'Beware the ides of March' an example of dramatic irony?
options: The audience knows Caesar will die on that date; he does not
questions.a: B) The audience knows Caesar will die on that date; he does not. The audience knows the history; the other options misread it.

questions.q: What does 'petty men' suggest?
options: Cassius wants Brutus to feel small and resentful
questions.a: C) Cassius wants Brutus to feel small and resentful. The contrast with the giant aims to stir resentment; the other options miss the manipulation.

questions.q: 'A story of suffering can move us' describes...
questions.a: A) pathos. Emotion is pathos; logic is logos; trust is ethos.

questions.q: Which sentence uses parallelism correctly?
options: He was brave, and loyal, wise.
He was brave, loyal and wise.
He was brave, loyal and acted wisely.
questions.a: B) He was brave, loyal and wise.. All three are adjectives; the second option breaks the pattern with a verb phrase; the third is unbalanced.

questions.q: What is the flaw in Brutus's 'serpent's egg' reasoning?
options: He has proof of Caesar's crimes
He punishes Caesar for what he might do, not what he has done
questions.a: C) He punishes Caesar for what he might do, not what he has done. He admits Caesar has done no wrong yet; the image replaces evidence with fear.

questions.q: Which is a subordinate clause?
questions.a: A) although Brutus was loyal. It begins with 'although' and cannot stand alone; the others are main clauses.

questions.q: Why is Act 3 scene 1 the turning point?
options: After the murder, power shifts and the conspirators begin to fall
questions.a: B) After the murder, power shifts and the conspirators begin to fall. The assassination changes the direction of the play; Caesar never becomes king and the play continues to Philippi.

questions.q: Which remedy fits 'nobody wants to say Wait'?
questions.a: C) Invite anyone to speak up. Inviting challenge counters group pressure; acting faster makes it worse.

questions.q: Which sentence has a dangling modifier?
options: Stabbed by his friends, the crowd mourned Caesar.
Stabbed by his friends, Caesar fell.
questions.a: A) Stabbed by his friends, the crowd mourned Caesar.. The crowd was not stabbed; the phrase must describe Caesar.

questions.q: Why does Antony keep saying 'Brutus is an honourable man'?
options: Repetition makes the phrase sound ironic, so the crowd doubts it
questions.a: B) Repetition makes the phrase sound ironic, so the crowd doubts it. Each repetition follows evidence of Caesar's goodness, so it becomes sarcastic; the other options miss the irony.

questions.q: Repeating 'we shall fight' at the start of lines is...
questions.a: C) anaphora. Anaphora repeats openings; the others are different methods.

questions.q: Which is a cleft sentence?
options: It was the will that changed everything.
questions.a: A) It was the will that changed everything.. 'It was... that' splits the sentence to stress 'the will'; the others are plain.

questions.q: Why does Antony save the will until the end?
options: To build to a climax that turns the crowd completely
questions.a: B) To build to a climax that turns the crowd completely. Saving the will creates a climax; the other options are untrue.

questions.q: What is Brutus's hamartia?
options: His naive belief that others are as honourable as he is
questions.a: C) His naive belief that others are as honourable as he is. His trust in honour makes him spare Antony and follow Cassius; he is neither greedy nor a coward.

questions.q: Which is the strongest thesis?
options: Shakespeare suggests that leaders fall when pride or honour blinds their judgement.
There are many leaders in the play.
questions.a: A) Shakespeare suggests that leaders fall when pride or honour blinds their judgement.. It makes an argument; the others only state facts.

questions.q: Which DIRT edit adds the most?
questions.a: C) Adding a Zoom in on 'honourable'. Only the Zoom in adds analysis; the others are cosmetic.

questions.q: In Animal Farm, who seizes power?
questions.a: B) Napoleon
